summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Research design for identifying sanctions regimes and export controls that affect Nepal's trade, banking and technology imports, with leads to the UN consolidated list, OFAC sanctions programmes and SDN search, US BIS EAR (Country Chart, Country Groups, Entity List), the EU Sanctions Map and FATF monitoring pages. Four channels are defined: direct designation of Nepali parties, EAR licence requirements for dual-use/advanced-computing imports, secondary-sanctions exposure through counterparties (Iran, Russia, DPRK-linked), and FATF-driven correspondent-banking de-risking. Whether any regime names Nepal is pending retrieval; no values were retrieved. Several leads use catalog base URLs because the session search budget was exhausted.

findings.claim: Q1a: Whether Nepal, or any Nepali person or entity, is designated under UN, US (OFAC), EU sanctions regimes or on the US BIS Entity List.
findings.note: Query each consolidated list for country=Nepal on a stated retrieval date; record list vintage. Leads 19B-L01..L05.

findings.claim: Q1b: US export-control treatment of Nepal - Country Group placement and Commerce Country Chart reasons for control applicable to Nepal, including advanced-computing/semiconductor rules.
findings.note: Retrieve 15 CFR Part 738 Supplement 1, Part 740 Supplement 1 and the current advanced-computing rules; record Federal Register vintage.

findings.claim: Q1c: Secondary-sanctions exposure via Nepal's counterparties - trade and payments with Iran, Russia and DPRK-linked parties (value by HS chapter and partner) and any remittance corridors from sanctioned jurisdictions.
findings.note: Requires Nepal customs partner tables (FY) for Iran and Russia and NRB payment-system guidance; no Nepal-specific lead located in r1.

findings.claim: Q1d: FATF increased-monitoring status of Nepal and its effect on correspondent banking - current listing status and action-plan items.
findings.note: Retrieve latest FATF plenary outcome after February 2025 (19B-L06, L07); correspondent-relationship counts are supervisory data (see 20D/16B gap).

findings.claim: FATF monitoring is not a sanctions regime but is included because it acts through the same compliance channel (correspondent banking, enhanced due diligence) on Nepal's banks.

An HS-to-ECCN concordance (16B-A3) will be built as a labelled assumption: EAR controls attach to items (ECCNs), not HS codes, so any estimate of the share of Nepal's imports subject to licence requirements is an estimate, not a fact.

data_gaps: No Nepal-specific primary lead located for trade/payments with sanctioned jurisdictions (customs partner tables for Iran/Russia to be requested via 21A/17A).
Current FATF status after February 2025 not verified.
NRB directives on sanctions screening and correspondent-banking guidance not located.

WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted during r1 before all lead searches were completed; leads marked 'NOT confirmed by web search' use catalog base URLs or known primary domains and must be verified on fetch.

assumptions.text: Only lawful compliance implications are analysed; no guidance on evading sanctions or controls is produced.
HS-to-ECCN concordance is an assumption to be documented (answers 16B-A3).

challenges.text: 16B-A3 assigns the HS-to-ECCN concordance to 19B; accepted, but EXP-19 must be labelled an estimate and its unit/period fixed once the EAR vintage is retrieved.
X28 (sanctions regimes relevant to counterparties) and FATF monitoring overlap; agree a single owner for correspondent-banking indicators to avoid double counting.
Add NRB FIU-Nepal and NRB directives as sources; catalog lacks a Nepal-side sanctions-screening authority.

uncertainty: High. No list has been queried; the applicability of each regime to Nepal is pending. Lists change frequently, so every result must carry a retrieval date. Several URLs unverified by search.
